The GoTo makes it decisive: a name that cannot be a label cannot be a GoTo target either, so a clean compile means label and a syntax error means reserved. Prompted by a maintainer's recollection that `New` is illegal as a Sub name. Recorded as a hypothesis rather than a fact, because that is what this file is for - the same kind of remembered rule has already been wrong twice here (the docs on Rem's separator, a reviewer on bracket-escaping). Predicting illegal, and measuring it either way.

`New` as a Sub NAME - a different position from a label, and one that need not agree with it. Measured illegal: "Expected: identifier", refused at the declaration rather than at any call site.

Worth pinning rather than filing as incidental, because the illegality is LOAD-BEARING for anyone extending this language: a dialect that wants `New` to name a constructor can only slot it in cleanly because VB6 leaves the name unavailable. A fact that other work depends on is exactly the kind that should be measured and recorded rather than remembered.

Raised from a maintainer's recollection, and recorded as a hypothesis first - the same shape of remembered rule has already been wrong twice in this corpus. This one held.

The control for the New case. `Nothing` is a literal rather than an operator, so if the two disagreed the rule would be about operators specifically. They do not disagree - both are refused with the same "Expected: identifier" - so it is simple reservation, not an ambiguity VB6 is avoiding at the call site.
